reader.requirement: At --std 85 an unqualified LINE-COUNTER in the Procedure Division must be refused when the program has more than one RD and accepted when it has one; in the Report Section an unqualified LINE-COUNTER must mean the counter of the report whose RD contains it, and another report's counter must be reachable only as LINE-COUNTER OF/IN that report-name (a qualifier naming no report refused).

reader.notes: CounterResolver.ReportOf is the one resolution of a counter to its report for both directions: OF/IN report-name, else the enclosing RD in the Report Section, else exactly one nearest report or COBOL2729. No edition test on the path; the same diagnostics appear at 2023. Messages cite §2023 at --std 85 (cosmetic).

refuter.evidence: The single-program cases conform. r8loc: an unqualified LINE-COUNTER in a USE BEFORE REPORTING declarative with two RDs drew COBOL2729 (line 27). From a contained program, LINE-COUNTER OF R1 for a non-GLOBAL R1 drew COBOL2729 (43), and PAGE-COUNTER with no reachable report drew COBOL2729 (45). r7glob (85-only: RD R1 IS GLOBAL with an inner program that has no RD): LINE-COUNTER, LINE-COUNTER OF R1 and PAGE-COUNTER IN R1 printed 'IN1 02 / IN2 02 / IN3 01'. The nested cases rest on a reading. (1) The reader's q85lcn, rerun here at 85, prints 'OUTER 01 / INNER 03': the outer program writes an unqualified LINE-COUNTER in its Procedure Division while its contained program specifies a second RD. In 1985 a source program textually contains its contained programs ('OK  §1985:X.2.1 ... A COBOL source program may contain other COBOL source programs'; 'OK  §1985:X.2.2 ... The end of a COBOL source program is indicated by either the end program header'). Read that way, the outer source program has two report description entries specified in it, and rule 9 ('OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.9 ... more than one report description entry is specified in the source program') requires qualification. (2) r9gl2 at 85: the outer has RD R1 IS GLOBAL, so its counters are global names ('OK  §1985:X.4.4.4 GR1'), and the inner has its own RD R2. The unqualified LINE-COUNTER at line 47 is accepted and silently resolved to R2 ('IN1 03', while R1's counter is 01). Two LINE-COUNTERs can be referenced in that program, and §1985:XIII.3.5.6 SR3 ('OK ... If more than one LINE-COUNTER exists in a program, LINE-COUNTER must be qualified by a report-name whenever it is referenced in the Procedure Division') plus the clause text of §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 ('Reserved words naming the special registers require qualification ... whenever a source program would result in more than one occurrence') can each be read to require qualification. The reader's verdict takes the per-program reading by way of §1985:X.1.3.8.2, but that convention governs condition-names, data-names, file-names, record-names and report-names, not special registers. The 1985 text does not settle which reading is right. At --std 2023 both programs are also accepted, but there 'source element' (§2023:8.4.2.2.3 SR9) excludes contained programs, so the 2023 text supports that behaviour and the 1985 text may not.
edition-sites-missed: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/CounterResolver.cs#ReportOf: no edition arm. The count of reachable reports for an unqualified Procedure Division counter (nearest scope first) is the same at 85 as at 2023, even though rule 9 counts RDs 'specified in the source program' in 1985 and 'in the source element' in 2023.
refuter.corrected: Under the literal 1985 reading this is NOT CONFORMING (under-rejects), cause (c). The 1985 'source program' includes contained programs, so (i) an unqualified Procedure Division LINE-COUNTER/PAGE-COUNTER in a program whose source program (contained programs included) specifies more than one RD, and (ii) an unqualified counter in a contained program that has its own RD and also sees a GLOBAL RD, would each need COBOL2729. The compiler accepts both and resolves to the nearest report. Under the reader's per-program reading it CONFORMS. Settle it with an adjudication note before closing the rule.

adjudication.reason: An unqualified LINE-COUNTER counts the report descriptions of the program it is written in (kb/Work PB5800): a recorded determination (register entry D-85-COUNTER-QUAL). The 1985 text leaves the count open (§1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.9, §1985:XIII.3.5.6 SR3); GnuCOBOL counts per program, and that decided it.
